scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] Myth vs. reality: 'The SBA guarantee protects me if my business fails.' The guaranty protects the lender, the borrower still owes the full debt, and owners of 20% or more generally sign a personal guaranty.
scripts.audience: First-time SBA borrowers (franchise buyers, acquisition buyers, growth owners) who read 'government-backed' as lower personal risk
scripts.problem: Viewers misread 'government-guaranteed' as protection for the borrower, and that changes how they weigh personal risk before they borrow.
scripts.amount_context: No deal size or loan amount used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned. The only figure is the twenty percent ownership threshold for personal guaranties (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
scripts.hook: The SBA guarantee isn't there to protect you. Here's who it protects.
scripts.script: The SBA guarantee isn't there to protect you. Here's who it protects. The myth: it's government-backed, so if my business fails, I'm covered. The reality: on an SBA seven-A loan, one of the SBA's loan programs, the SBA guarantees part of the loan to the lender. If the borrower defaults, the lender can ask the SBA to buy that guaranteed portion. You still owe the full debt. Now the twist. Owners of twenty percent or more generally must sign a full, unlimited personal guarantee. That means you're personally responsible for repaying if the business can't. And after a default, the SBA may use legal means to recover what's still owed. That's as of October twenty twenty-six, and subject to change. None of this means don't borrow. It means borrow with clear eyes. Share this with your business partner before you both sign.
scripts.cta: Share this with your business partner before you both sign.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando directo a cámara, tono sereno y sin dramatismo. Pausa breve después de 'Here's who it protects' para generar curiosidad. Cambia de postura o da un paso leve al decir 'Now the twist'. Habla más despacio en la parte del personal guarantee. Termina con una sonrisa tranquila, que no se vea como advertencia alarmista.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V17 solo se toma el mecanismo de 'fijar expectativas realistas' sobre los préstamos SBA. No se copian frases, guion ni historia del creador. El enfoque mito/realidad sobre a quién protege la garantía es original.

fact_refs.claim: The SBA guarantees part of a 7(a) loan to the lender; on default the lender can ask the SBA to buy the guaranteed portion; the borrower still owes the full debt.
Owners of 20% or more generally must give a full, unlimited personal guaranty (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
After a default the remaining debt is still owed and the SBA may use all legal means available to recover it.

scripts.why_selected_es: Corrige una idea equivocada muy común con un giro claro (el personal guarantee). Es fácil de compartir entre socios o compradores antes de firmar, y no repite el mito de 'la SBA presta el dinero' de ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Compartidos y envíos por DM a terceros como métrica principal. Después, retención hasta el giro (~20 s) y guardados. Las vistas no cuentan como leads.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] Inside the SBA 504 structure: bank first lien, CDC second lien funded by an SBA-guaranteed debenture, and borrower equity, plus who a CDC is.
scripts.audience: Established owners planning to buy owner-occupied real estate or major equipment; acquisition buyers whose deal includes real estate
scripts.problem: People hear '504' without knowing it means two lenders plus their own equity, so term sheets are confusing and they don't know who to talk to first.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amount used. Percentages only (fifty / forty / ten, fifteen and twenty percent borrower contribution), as of Oct 2026, subject to change. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: An SBA five-oh-four loan is really three pieces of money stacked together.
scripts.script: An SBA five-oh-four loan is really three pieces of money stacked together. Layer one: a third-party lender, usually a bank, typically finances fifty percent of the project and holds the first lien, meaning first claim on the asset. Layer two: up to forty percent comes from a CDC, with a second lien. It's funded by a debenture, a type of bond, that the SBA guarantees one hundred percent. Layer three is you. At least ten percent equity, typically. It goes up to fifteen percent if the business has less than two years of history or the property is special-purpose, built for one specific use, and twenty percent if both apply. So who is the CDC? A Certified Development Company: a nonprofit the SBA certifies and regulates to deliver five-oh-four loans. As of October twenty twenty-six, subject to change. Confirm with your lender. Save this for your next property conversation.
scripts.cta: Save this for your next property conversation.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, energía tranquila de explicador. Usa las manos para 'apilar' tres capas a distintas alturas (una por capa) y vuelve a ese gesto en cada 'Layer'. Pausa breve antes de 'So who is the CDC?' y baja el ritmo para la definición. Mira a cámara todo el tiempo.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V28 solo se toma la idea de explicar el programa 504 aplicado a la compra de inmuebles. No se copia el nicho (wedding venues), las frases ni la cifra de 'up to $5 million', que no está verificada en SBA.gov y se deja fuera.

fact_refs.claim: In a 504 loan, a third-party lender (usually a bank) holds a first lien, a CDC holds a second lien funded by a debenture the SBA guarantees 100%, and the borrower contributes equity.
Typical split 50% lender, up to 40% CDC, at least 10% borrower; 15% if under two years of operating history or special-purpose property; 20% if both (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
A CDC is a nonprofit certified and regulated by the SBA to deliver 504 loans.

scripts.why_selected_es: Es una explicación de referencia (las tres capas y los porcentajes) que el público quiere guardar para cuando analice un inmueble. Profundiza en la estructura sin repetir la comparación 7(a) vs 504 de ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados como métrica principal. Después, retención hasta la definición de CDC y DMs calificados de dueños con proyectos inmobiliarios. Las vistas no son leads.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] SBA Express vs. standard 7(a): what 'Express' changes (lender's delegated decision, smaller maximum, lower guaranty share) and what it does not mean (fast approval).
scripts.audience: Owners looking for smaller growth or working-capital loans who have seen 'SBA Express' advertised
scripts.problem: The program name suggests guaranteed speed, so owners may choose a product by its name instead of by loan size and fit.
scripts.amount_context: Program maximums only: five hundred thousand dollars (SBA Express) and five million dollars (standard 7(a)), plus the one hundred fifty thousand dollar guaranty threshold, as of Oct 2026, subject to change. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: Express doesn't mean what most people think.
scripts.script: Express doesn't mean what most people think. It's not a promise of fast approval. SBA Express is a version of the seven-A loan program, and here's what changes. First, who decides. Express lenders have delegated authority, so they make the credit decision using their own procedures, then send the guarantee request to the SBA. Second, size. As of October twenty twenty-six, Express goes up to five hundred thousand dollars. Standard seven-A goes up to five million dollars. Third, the guarantee. Express carries a fifty percent guarantee to the lender. Standard seven-A is up to eighty-five percent for loans of one hundred fifty thousand dollars or less, and seventy-five percent above that. What stays the same? A lender still has to approve your loan, and nothing about the name guarantees speed. These figures can change, so confirm with your lender. Share this with someone comparing SBA options.
scripts.cta: Share this with someone comparing SBA options.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono seguro y algo pícaro en el hook, sin exagerar. Marca con los dedos 'First, Second, Third'. Pausa clara antes de 'What stays the same?' y mira fijo a cámara en 'nothing about the name guarantees speed'. Ritmo constante, sin apurarse en las cifras.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Guion original. No se basa en ninguna referencia de creador; la comparación Express vs 7(a) estándar se construyó solo con datos verificados.

fact_refs.claim: SBA Express lenders have delegated authority, decide on credit using their own procedures and submit the guaranty request to the SBA.
SBA Express maximum is $500,000 (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
Standard 7(a) maximum is $5 million (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
SBA Express guaranty is 50%; standard 7(a) is up to 85% for loans of $150,000 or less and 75% above (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).

scripts.why_selected_es: El término 'SBA Express' se busca y se publicita mucho; aclarar qué significa realmente atrae a nuevos públicos (descubrimiento) y refuerza la confianza al evitar promesas de rapidez. No se cubrió ayer.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Alcance a no seguidores, visitas al perfil y nuevos seguidores como señales de descubrimiento. Después, compartidos y retención hasta 'What stays the same?'. Las vistas no son leads.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] 'What happens after I apply for an SBA loan?' Stage map: underwriting, SBA guaranty step (delegated or not), closing requirements, closing and funding. No timelines.
scripts.audience: Borrowers about to apply or who have just applied (franchise buyers, acquisition buyers, growth owners)
scripts.problem: Not knowing what comes after submission creates anxiety and missed requests; borrowers don't expect closing requirements such as a business valuation.
scripts.amount_context: No dollar amount used. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: You hit submit on your SBA loan application. Then what?
scripts.script: You hit submit on your SBA loan application. Then what? Here's the general path, and it varies by lender and deal. Stage one: underwriting. The lender reviews your application and decides on the loan. Stage two: the SBA step. Some lenders have delegated authority, meaning they approve the loan themselves and submit it electronically for an SBA loan number. Other lenders send it to an SBA processing center, which reviews it and issues the loan number if approved. Stage three is where surprises show up: closing requirements. As of October twenty twenty-six, subject to change, buying a business generally requires an independent business valuation. If an agent is paid, there's a fee disclosure form. Insurance and lien filings, the lender's recorded claim on assets, are common. Stage four: closing and funding. No stage comes with a guaranteed timeline. Which stage feels least clear? Tell us in a DM.
scripts.cta: Which stage feels least clear? Tell us in a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, tono empático, como quien acompaña a alguien ansioso. En el hook, gesto breve de 'enviar' con la mano y pausa en 'Then what?'. Marca cada etapa con los dedos. Baja un poco la voz y acércate a cámara en 'Stage three is where surprises show up' para sostener la atención. Cierra con una pregunta genuina, mirando a cámara.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V17 solo se toma el mecanismo de fijar expectativas ('el proceso puede ser exhaustivo'). Se adapta como mapa de etapas posterior a la solicitud; no se copian frases ni contenido del creador.

fact_refs.claim: The lender underwrites; delegated lenders approve and submit via E-Tran where the SBA assigns a loan number; for other lenders the SBA's processing center reviews and issues the loan number if approved.
Under SOP 50 10 8.1 (effective for loan numbers on or after Oct 1, 2026), change-of-ownership deals require an independent business valuation (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
If an agent is paid in connection with the loan, SBA Form 159 (Fee Disclosure and Compensation Agreement) is required.
Insurance and lien filings are commonly part of closing; varies by lender and deal.

scripts.why_selected_es: El formato de etapas con un bucle abierto ('stage three is where surprises show up') mantiene la atención hasta el final y reduce la ansiedad de quien ya aplicó. Va más allá de lo cubierto ayer (objeción del papeleo y elección de prestamista). Se omitió la commitment letter por no estar verificada.

scripts.topic: [Pillar: SBA loans explained] Objection: 'I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan.' How SBA collateral expectations work by loan size, and when personal real estate may come into play.
scripts.audience: Owners and buyers without much hard collateral (service businesses, first-time buyers) who rule themselves out of SBA loans
scripts.problem: People assume collateral disqualifies them and never start a conversation; others don't realize equity in personal real estate may be requested.
scripts.amount_context: Program collateral thresholds only: fifty thousand dollars and three hundred fifty thousand dollars for 7(a), as of Oct 2026, subject to change. The provisional ~USD 300,000 figure is not mentioned.
scripts.hook: "I don't have enough collateral for an SBA loan." Let's look at what the rule says.
scripts.script: "I don't have enough collateral for an SBA loan." Let's look at what the rule says. Collateral means assets a lender can claim if the loan isn't repaid. Under current SBA policy, a lender isn't supposed to decline an otherwise eligible loan just because collateral falls short. So, not an automatic no. But here's the catch. For seven-A loans of fifty thousand dollars or less, no collateral is required. Above that, up to three hundred fifty thousand dollars, the lender follows its own collateral policy. For larger loans, lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible. And if business assets don't cover it, that can include equity in your personal real estate, sometimes your home. These thresholds are as of October twenty twenty-six, subject to change, and the lender still makes the credit decision. Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio. Di la objeción del hook con tono de cita (cejas levemente arriba), luego cambia a un tono cálido y seguro. Pausa en 'So, not an automatic no.' y otra en 'But here's the catch.' Habla despacio en los umbrales. En la parte de la casa personal, tono honesto, sin alarmar. Cierra con una invitación tranquila mirando a cámara.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Guion original, sin referencia de creador. La estructura objeción + 'sí, pero' se construyó solo con los datos verificados sobre colateral.

fact_refs.claim: Under SOP 50 10 8, an otherwise-eligible loan is not to be declined solely because collateral is inadequate (paraphrased).

No collateral required for 7(a) loans of $50,000 or less; from $50,001 to $350,000 lenders follow their own policy for similar non-SBA loans; above that lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible (as of Oct 2026, subject to change).
If business assets don't fully secure a larger loan, lenders must take available equity in owners' personal real estate (threshold not stated; confirm under SOP 50 10 8.1).
The lender still makes the credit decision.

scripts.why_selected_es: Responde a una objeción que hace que muchos compradores y dueños se descarten solos. Abre una conversación calificada por DM sin prometer aprobación. Ningún guion de ayer trató el colateral.

scripts.topic: [SBA loans explained] Objection: 'I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan.' How SBA collateral rules work by loan size, as of October 2026
scripts.audience: Owners and buyers without much hard collateral (service businesses, first-time buyers) who rule themselves out of SBA loans
scripts.problem: People assume they can't qualify because of collateral, so they never have the conversation. Others don't realize their personal home equity may come into play on larger loans.
scripts.amount_context: SBA program thresholds only (as of Oct 2026, subject to change): $50,000; $350,000; $500,000 for SBA Express. These are not deal-size figures and the provisional ~$300,000 is not used.
scripts.hook: "I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan." Here's what the rules say.
scripts.script: "I don't have enough collateral, so I can't get an SBA loan." Here's what the rules say. As of October twenty twenty-six, and subject to change: for seven-A loans of fifty thousand dollars or less, the SBA doesn't require collateral. Between that and three hundred fifty thousand, lenders follow their own collateral policy for similar loans. For SBA Express, that lender-policy range goes up to five hundred thousand. Above those amounts, lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible. And here's the key part: an otherwise eligible loan isn't supposed to be declined only because collateral falls short. But that's not a yes. The lender still decides, so confirm with yours. And on larger loans, if business assets don't cover it, lenders may need to look at equity in your personal real estate. Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.cta: Not sure how your collateral picture fits? Send us a DM.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio, mirando a cámara. Dice la objeción con tono de cliente, algo escéptico, y luego hace una pausa de un segundo antes de 'Here's what the rules say'. Al dar los tramos, marca con la mano tres niveles (bajo, medio, alto). Baja el ritmo y pone voz seria en 'But that's not a yes'. Cierre cálido y sin prisa.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: Original. No se adapta ningún video de referencia. Se usa el mecanismo genérico de objeción y luego un 'sí, pero' en dos partes.

fact_refs.claim: As of Oct 2026: no collateral required for 7(a) loans of $50,000 or less; from $50,001 to $350,000 lenders follow their own policy for similar non-SBA loans; above that, lenders must take available collateral to the maximum extent possible
SBA Express lenders may apply their own collateral policy for loans over $50,000 up to $500,000
An otherwise-eligible loan is not to be declined solely because collateral is inadequate (paraphrased, not quoted)

If business assets don't fully secure a larger loan, lenders must take available equity in owners' personal real estate (phrased with 'may', 25% threshold omitted; confirm under SOP 50 10 8.1 before airing)

scripts.why_selected_es: Nadie lo cubrió ayer. Es una objeción que hace que buena gente se autodescarte, y responderla con la regla real abre conversaciones calificadas sin prometer aprobación.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: DMs calificados que mencionen garantías o colateral, retención hasta el 'But that's not a yes', guardados y visitas al perfil. Las vistas no cuentan como leads.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Hypothetical scenario: royalties and the ad fund come off monthly sales before rent, payroll and the loan payment
scripts.audience: Prospective franchisees comparing brands who focus on revenue claims
scripts.problem: Buyers judge a franchise by gross sales and underestimate ongoing fees calculated on revenue, which shrinks the cash left for debt service.
scripts.amount_context: Hypothetical: $50,000 in monthly gross sales, a hypothetical 6% royalty ($3,000) and a hypothetical 2% ad fund ($1,000). Not real brand data and not the provisional deal-size figure.
scripts.hook: Your franchise does fifty thousand dollars in sales this month. Here's what comes off the top before anything else gets paid.
scripts.script: Your franchise does fifty thousand dollars in sales this month. Here's what comes off the top before anything else gets paid. This is a hypothetical, with round numbers. Say the royalty, your ongoing fee to the franchisor, is six percent of gross sales. That's three thousand dollars gone. Say the ad fund is two percent. Another thousand. Now you're at forty-six thousand, and you haven't paid rent, payroll, supplies or utilities yet. And then the loan payment. That comes out of whatever's left after all of that. The Federal Trade Commission's franchise guide notes royalties may be based on a percentage of your gross income, even in a month you lose money. Your real fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six of the franchise disclosure document. Save this, and run your own numbers before you compare brands.
scripts.cta: Save this, and run your own numbers before you compare brands.
scripts.recording_notes_es: Plano medio con energía tranquila. En cada resta, pausa breve, como si contara con los dedos. Pausa marcada antes de 'And then the loan payment' para crear expectativa. Mirada directa y tono serio en la parte de la FTC. Sonrisa leve en el cierre.
scripts.adaptation_note_es: De V21 solo se toma el mecanismo de explicar la jerga de las regalías. No se copia texto ni historia. Se suma una 'cascada' hipotética propia y la referencia oficial a Item 6.

fact_refs.claim: FDD Item 6 discloses other recurring or occasional fees paid to the franchisor, such as royalties and advertising fees
The FTC guide says royalties may be based on a percentage of weekly or monthly gross income, even if you are losing money (paraphrased)
$50,000 sales, 6% royalty, 2% ad fund and the resulting $46,000 are hypothetical round numbers

scripts.why_selected_es: Es un tema de flujo de caja continuo (Item 6) que no cubrimos ayer (Item 7/9). La cascada numérica retiene y da ganas de guardar el video para hacer las propias cuentas.
scripts.what_to_measure_es: Guardados, retención hasta el 'And then the loan payment', compartidos y DMs sobre franquicias. Las vistas no son leads.

scripts.topic: [Buying a franchise] Resale franchise vs. new unit: operating history vs. projections, transfer terms and fee, valuation on a change of ownership, Franchise Directory
scripts.audience: Prospective franchisees deciding between a resale and a new unit within the next year
scripts.problem: Buyers don't realize a resale is a transfer and a change of ownership with its own steps, while a new unit relies only on projections.
scripts.amount_context: No amounts used.
scripts.hook: Buying an existing franchise location and opening a new one are two different financing conversations.
scripts.script: Buying an existing franchise location and opening a new one are two different financing conversations. A new unit has no track record, so the numbers are projections. A resale comes with an operating history you can review. A resale is also a transfer. Item seventeen of the franchise disclosure document summarizes the transfer terms, and Item six may list a transfer fee. And it's a change of ownership. For either path, if you want SBA financing, the brand has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory. Check the current list. Line three: working capital, the cash to cover day-to-day costs, forty thousand, backed by your monthly expense budget. Line four: closing costs and fees, ten thousand, backed by written estimates. Total uses: two hundred fifty thousand. Then the other side: your loan request plus your own cash has to add up to that same number. If the two columns don't match, something's missing. scripts.hook: "The business is borrowing, not me."
scripts.script: "The business is borrowing, not me." Fair point. But with an SBA loan, your personal finances are part of the picture. Here's why, in three parts. One: the personal guaranty. As of October twenty twenty-six, owners of twenty percent or more generally must give a full personal guaranty. That means you personally back the loan. Two: the personal financial statement. That's SBA Form four-thirteen. It's completed by owners of twenty percent or more, by any guarantor, and by certain others like proprietors and general partners. Three: the credit elsewhere test. Lenders must check that the business and its owners of twenty percent or more don't have readily available funds that make the SBA loan unnecessary. There are reasonable exceptions. It's built into the program. Confirm the details with your lender. Share this with anyone buying a business with you.

input.summary_es: Revisé los diez guiones reescritos solo con el texto del input, sin abrir archivos, como se pidió. Siete quedan listos para grabar (R06, R08, R09, R10, R16, R17, R19) y tres pendientes (R05, R07, R18). Todos duran entre 50 y 58 segundos. Ninguno tiene dígitos en el texto hablado, promesas de aprobación, recursos de CTA inexistentes ni notas de edición, overlays o B-roll. Las cifras en dólares están etiquetadas como hipotéticas o como umbrales del programa. Motivos de los pendientes: (1) R05 usa la regla sobre bienes inmuebles personales y los tramos de colateral, que el equipo de investigación pidió confirmar en la SOP 50 10 8.1 antes de usarlos. (2) R07 presenta como regla vigente la valuación independiente obligatoria, que solo tiene fuente de la industria y quedó marcada como 'confirmar antes de publicar'. Además omite que la regla del Franchise Directory aplica a marcas que cumplen la definición de franquicia de la FTC. (3) R18 tiene un error de cálculo en la fila hipotética: cuarenta mil dólares a mil por mes no se terminan de pagar en 2029. Esto le resta credibilidad a un asesor financiero. Mantengo el top 5 anterior. R05 sería candidato al quinto puesto por su potencial para generar conversaciones calificadas, pero por ahora sigue pendiente. R13 y los demás guiones aprobados antes no se volvieron a revisar en detalle en esta pasada.

issues_es: La frase 'on larger loans, if business assets don't cover it, lenders may need to look at equity in your personal real estate' viene de un snippet de fuente mixta. La investigación pide expresamente 'Confirm under 8.1 before using', y el propio fact_ref dice 'confirm before airing'. Arreglo: confirmarla en la SOP 50 10 8.1 antes de grabar o quitar la frase.

Los tramos de colateral (cincuenta mil, trescientos cincuenta mil y quinientos mil para Express) salen de resúmenes de la industria sobre la SOP 50 10 8, con la nota 'confirm in 8.1'. Sin embargo, el guion los fecha 'As of October twenty twenty-six', cuando ya rige la 8.1. Arreglo: confirmarlos en la 8.1 o reformular como 'Under the SBA's SOP 50 10 8 rules, and subject to change, ...', sin atribuirlos a octubre de 2026.
No bloqueante: 'Here's what the rules say' anticipa una cita textual. Como la regla de no rechazar solo por falta de colateral está parafraseada, conviene 'Here's how the rules work'.

No bloqueante: 'Your real fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six' exagera, porque la cuota inicial de franquicia está en el Item 5. Arreglo: 'Your ongoing fees, and how each one is calculated, are listed in Item six'.

No bloqueante: 'before anything else gets paid' sugiere un orden de pago real. Se puede suavizar con 'Here's what comes off the top, on paper, before anything else'. El dos por ciento del fondo de publicidad ya está marcado como hipotético, así que no contradice la guía de la investigación.

La valuación independiente obligatoria en todo cambio de propiedad bajo la 8.1 tiene solo fuente de la industria (S10). La investigación indica 'reportedly' y 'confirm before airing'. Decirle al espectador 'Confirm it with your lender' no sustituye esa verificación interna. Arreglo: confirmarlo en el texto oficial de la SOP 50 10 8.1 antes de grabar o quitar la frase.

'For either path, if you want SBA financing, the brand has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory' omite la condición. Arreglo: 'if the brand meets the Federal Trade Commission's franchise definition, it has to be on the SBA Franchise Directory', como ya se hace en R10.

No bloqueante: 'units two and three each need their own funding, on their own timeline' suena absoluto, porque algunas estructuras financian varias unidades juntas. Sugerencia: 'units two and three still have to be funded, on the schedule's timeline, and none of that comes with the signature'.
No bloqueante: 'the franchise rules apply' es vago. Conviene 'the Federal Trade Commission's Franchise Rule generally applies', manteniendo la mención de las exenciones.

No bloqueante: 'your loan request plus your own cash has to add up' deja fuera la financiación del vendedor, que importa en adquisiciones. Sugerencia: 'your loan request, your own cash and any other sources, like seller financing, should add up to that same number'. Así queda como práctica común y no como regla. La suma (ciento veinte, ochenta, cuarenta y diez mil, total doscientos cincuenta mil) es correcta y está etiquetada como hipotética.
No bloqueante: 'use it as your outline' choca con la advertencia de que la guía tiene más secciones. Sugerencia: 'Save this as a starting outline'.

Error de cálculo en la fila hipotética: 'forty thousand dollars remaining, one thousand a month, paid off in twenty twenty-nine'. Cuarenta pagos de mil desde octubre de 2026 llegan a 2030, y más tarde aún con intereses. Arreglo: cambiar a 'final payment in twenty thirty', reducir el saldo (por ejemplo, 'twenty-five thousand remaining ... paid off in twenty twenty-nine') o quitar el año.
No bloqueante: el CTA pide responder en comentarios. Está permitido, pero el canal aprobado para conversión es el DM. Se puede sumar 'or send us a DM'.

No bloqueante: la prueba de 'credit elsewhere' se respalda en la SOP 50 10 8, y no se confirmó si sigue igual en la 8.1. El guion no la fecha, lo cual es correcto. Conviene no agregarle 'As of October twenty twenty-six' y mantener 'Confirm the details with your lender'.

top5.reason_es: Sigue siendo el guion con más probabilidades de convertir. El CTA filtra por intención y por plazo, y el caso A/B se presenta como hipotético, sin prometer aprobación.
Habla a dueños actuales en una situación urgente y concreta, la salida de un socio, que es una necesidad de financiación real y lleva a DMs calificados.
La cascada hipotética de regalías y fondo de publicidad retiene y se guarda. Además, ahora está lista para grabar, con cifras claramente etiquetadas y la referencia oficial a la FTC y al Item 6.

Abre un segmento calificado poco tratado, los dueños independientes que piensan convertirse en franquicia. Está listo para grabar, con la condición del Franchise Directory bien planteada, y cada caso lleva naturalmente a un DM.

Es una plantilla práctica que sirve a todos los tipos de prestatario, con una suma hipotética correcta y muy guardable. Está listo para grabar. R05 podría reemplazarlo cuando se confirme en la SOP 8.1.
